## Main estimation results

**Primary specification** — dep. var. = growth of log GNI pc; exposure = annual change in education-investment share (pp of GNI); OLS with Newey-West(4) SEs. Coefficient = change in annual per-capita growth per +1 pp of GNI redirected to education.

| Spec | Group | b | SE | t | p | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 `dy~Δedu` | LMC | +0.0219 | 0.0104 | 2.11 | .035 | 40 |
| **A2 `dy~Δedu+exp_growth` (PRIMARY)** | **LMC** | **+0.0151** | **0.0056** | **2.70** | **.007** | **40** |
| A3 A2 + primary & secondary GER | LMC | +0.0326 | 0.0072 | 4.53 | <.001 | 40 |
| A4 window ≥1991 | LMC | −0.0312 | 0.0445 | −0.70 | .484 | 25 |
| A5 distributed lag: Δedu_t | LMC | −0.0063 | 0.0196 | −0.32 | .750 | 39 |
| A5 distributed lag: Δedu_{t−1} | LMC | −0.0131 | 0.0103 | −1.27 | .203 | 39 |
| A5 **cumulative** (b₀+b₁) | LMC | −0.0193 | 0.0266 | −0.73 | .468 | 39 |
| A6 `dy~edu_{t−1}` (level→growth) | LMC | −0.0330 | 0.0185 | −1.78 | .075 | 40 |
| A1 `dy~Δedu` | SSA | **−0.0516** | 0.0236 | −2.18 | .029 | **4** |
| A2 `dy~Δedu+exp_growth` | SSA | **+0.0408** | 0.0330 | 1.24 | .433 | **4** |
| A6 `dy~edu_{t−1}` | SSA | −0.0200 | 0.0164 | −1.22 | .223 | 4 |
| A3 (with GERs) | SSA | *INSUFFICIENT SUPPORT* | | | | 4 |

**Distributed lag:** adding Δedu_{t−1} **does change the sign and eliminates the LMC slope** — current −0.0063, lagged −0.0131, cumulative −0.0193 (t=−0.73). The positive contemporaneous association does not survive a two-year lag structure.

**Levels contrast (spurious, labeled as such):** LMC `log GNIpc ~ edu + trend` → edu −0.2002 (SE 0.0658, t=−3.04), R²=0.919, **DW=0.52**; SSA (n=5) edu −0.0662 (SE 0.0315). Not effect estimates.

**Group comparison:** interaction `Δedu×SSA` = −0.0735 with NW(4) (SE 0.0172, t=−4.28) **but classical SE 0.1418, t=−0.52** — the apparent significance is a HAC artifact from 4 SSA rows; I do not report it as significant. Chow F(2,40)=0.134, p=0.875 (n=44, only 4 SSA rows). Naive slope gap −0.0735 (SE 0.0258, t=−2.85), but SEs are not comparable across n=4 vs n=40. Framed as power limitation, not equivalence.

**Robustness table** (`analysis/robustness_table.csv`, 13 variants × 2 groups): winsorizing exports ±20pp → +0.0157 (t=2.99); HAC lags 1/8 → SE 0.0150/0.0103; symmetric 2011–15 → −0.1194 (t=−5.83, n=5); dropping SSA year 2012 leaves LMC unchanged (+0.0151) but makes SSA unidentifiable (n=3); raw exports kept in headline as you directed.

**Inference quality — important new finding:** leave-one-year-out range for LMC A1 is **[−0.0049, +0.0293]**. Dropping **1976 alone** flips A1 to −0.0049 and A2 to +0.0017. A stationary block bootstrap (mean block 5) gives A2 95% CI **[−0.0096, +0.0332]**, bootstrap p=0.16 (P(b>0)=0.92); A3 survives (CI [+0.003,+0.052], p=0.028) but GERs are post-treatment. Subperiods split hard: 1976–90 +0.0368 (t=4.37, n=15) vs 1991–2015 −0.0312 (t=−0.70, n=25).

**Mechanism/descriptives:** SSA spends **+0.80 pp of GNI** more than LMC (1975–2015), yet 2015 GNI pc $1,634 vs $1,965, mean growth 1.24%/yr vs 2.01%/yr, secondary GER 43.4 vs 64.5. Reduced form `ΔGER ~ Δedu` is negative/insignificant in both groups (LMC secondary −0.786, t=−2.71).

## Submitted hypothesis

> Among the two groups in this dataset, **the Lower-middle-income aggregate shows the larger and better-supported positive association between rising education expenditure and per-capita output, and Sub-Saharan Africa shows the weaker one** — but the association is far weaker than the raw levels fit suggests, and it is not robust enough to support a causal claim. Using the only available proxies (outcome = GNI per capita, constant 2015 US$, rather than the brief's "GDP, 2010 US$"; exposure = "Adjusted savings: education expenditure," % of GNI, not a government budget share; "developing countries" = the LMC aggregate), a one-percentage-point increase in the share of GNI directed to education is associated with about **+1.5 percentage points of annual per-capita growth in LMC countries** (b=+0.0151, SE=0.0056, t=2.70, n=40, Newey-West(4)), whereas for Sub-Saharan Africa the corresponding slope is **unstable and not distinguishable from zero** (b=−0.0516, SE=0.0236, n=4 without controls; sign flips to +0.0408, SE=0.0330, t=1.24 once export growth is added; n=4 because SSA per-capita output exists only for 2011–2015). That SSA ordering is bounded by three facts: the LMC positive slope reverses sign under a two-year distributed lag (cumulative −0.0193, t=−0.73), disappears in the 1991–2015 subsample (−0.0312, t=−0.70), and is driven by a single year (dropping 1976 gives +0.0017; block-bootstrap 95% CI [−0.010, +0.033], p=0.16). The interaction between the education-share change and an SSA dummy is not interpretable (only 4 of 44 rows are SSA; Chow F(2,40)=0.134, p=0.875), so equality of slopes can be neither established nor rejected. Descriptively, SSA sustained a **higher** education-investment share than LMC (+0.80 pp of GNI on average 1975–2015, +0.25 pp even in 2011–2015) while ending 2015 **lower** in per-capita output ($1,634 vs $1,965), slower-growing (1.24%/yr vs 2.01%/yr) and far behind in secondary enrollment (gross 43.4 vs 64.5) — so higher education spending in SSA is associated with no relative per-capita-output advantage. Levels regressions that appear to show large negative effects (LMC edu −0.2002, t=−3.04, R²=0.92) are spurious common-trend artifacts (DW=0.52) and should not be read as effects. All estimates are associations from two overlapping WDI aggregate series in which the exposure's denominator is the outcome, so reverse causality and mechanical share effects remain unresolved.

**Workflow:** wide WDI reshape → tidy 2×41 panel (`analysis/panel_tidy.csv`) → coverage/missingness audit → primary differenced growth models with Newey-West(4) per group → distributed-lag and cumulative test → levels contrast flagged as spurious → interaction + Chow with classical-vs-HAC SE comparison → 13-variant robustness table → leave-one-year-out and stationary block bootstrap → enrollment/equity descriptives as mechanism.

**Limitations:** SSA rests on 4 growth observations; exposure denominator is the outcome (mechanical share + reverse causality, stated per your instruction, not solved); SSA/LMC membership overlap; 1976 leverage; export-growth outliers (SSF 2011 = −43.3 retained in headline); no fixed effects/instruments possible at N=2; bootstrap CIs unreliable at n=4.
